subject: ventures/uk-vat-flat-rate-scheme-calculator
professional: a UK chartered accountant / VAT adviser who files Flat Rate Scheme returns; checks first the VAT Notice 733 sector percentage table, the 1% first-year discount (including on the 16.5% limited cost rate), the limited cost trader test and what counts as relevant goods, the flat-rate turnover base, the £150k join / £230k leave limits and the £2,000 capital-asset reclaim

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs directly with node -e on 9 input sets. Arithmetic is right where the rule is right: general builder 100k ex VAT, goods 20k, first year -> 8.5% x 120,000 = 10,200 FRS vs 20,000-4,000 = 16,000 standard (hand: identical); LCT boundary at 50k turnover (2% of 60,000 gross = 1,200) flips correctly between goods 999 ex (1,198.80 inc, LCT) and 1,000 ex (1,200 inc, sector rate); capital asset 1,666.67 ex = 2,000.00 inc is reclaimed (333.33), 1,666.66 is not. Wrong where the rule is wrong: in the first year of registration HMRC's 1% reduction applies to the 16.5% limited cost rate too (15.5%; VAT Notice 733 newly-registered discount, GOV.UK 'VAT Flat Rate Scheme: how much you pay'; not fetched live, gov.uk 403 through the proxy), but the tool keeps 16.5%: IT consultant 60k, goods 300, other purchases 1,000, first year -> tool 11,880 FRS, 'Standard wins by £140'; correct 15.5% x 72,000 = 11,160, FRS wins by £580 (decision flips). The sector table has 52 rows; every rate checked matches the current (April 2017) table, but 'Catering services including restaurants and takeaways' (12.5%) and 'Any other activity not listed elsewhere' (12%) are missing. Above the limits the headline still says 'Flat Rate Scheme wins by £4,200' for a business at £240,000 VAT-inclusive that must leave.
evidence.completeness: README/page claim: sector flat rate (works, but 2 HMRC categories missing, so a restaurant cannot pick its trade); 16.5% LCT test (works, annual only, no per-period £250/quarter test); 1% first-year discount (works on sector rate, deliberately not on LCT, which is the wrong rule); capital asset reclaim (works, boundary right); join and leave limits (join works; leave is only mentioned inside the >£150k join finding and never stops the headline from recommending FRS). Download and print wired in index.html. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture dir: 23 tests, 23 pass (calc, page and usage). Seeded 5 mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 survived (LCT 2% comparison < -> <=; capital >= -> >; Management consultancy 14 -> 12), 2 caught (LCT £1,000 -> £250; first-year 1 -> 2 points). No test pins any boundary or the sector table against a source.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (115 lines), index.html, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Single compute() with validation, finite/negative checks, rounding helper, escaped output. '60,000' is rejected rather than parsed (the page input is type=number so the browser mostly prevents it). firstYear finding text and the LCT choice are hardcoded together. Clean for its size; no dead code.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty and 'not tax advice' present (index.html:110, calc.mjs summaryText). 'Covers ... the 1% first-year discount ... and the join and leave turnover limits' (index.html:87) is only partly backed: the discount is withheld from the LCT rate and leave is not modelled. README 'you know whether to join (or leave) the Flat Rate Scheme' overclaims given the wrong first-year LCT rate and missing sectors. VENTURE.yaml honestly records the rates were 'remembered without network access' and never verified since. Assumptions (standard-rated sales only) are stated on the page.
evidence.fitness: Walked a newly registered IT contractor through the page: it applies 16.5% and tells them standard accounting is better when the correct 15.5% makes FRS better, the exact decision the tool exists for. A restaurant or takeaway cannot select its sector. A food retailer (sales and goods mostly zero-rated) gets 'FRS wins' because the tool grosses up everything at 20% (disclosed limit). A plain standard-rated service business past its first year gets a sound answer.
evidence.domain: Against VAT Notice 733 (cited from knowledge, not fetched): sector rates that exist match; LCT test (2% of VAT-inclusive turnover or £1,000 a year, strict less-than, VAT-inclusive goods) matches for the annual case; £150k ex-VAT join and £2,000 inc-VAT capital rule match. Departs on: 1% first-year discount on the LCT rate; leave test (£230k inc VAT, unless expected below £191,500) not applied; per-period LCT test approximated annually; relevant-goods guidance omits vehicle parts and the resale/hire exclusion; flat-rate turnover including exempt/zero-rated sales not modelled (disclosed).

checks.method: HMRC VAT Notice 733, newly-registered 1% reduction applies to the appropriate percentage including 16.5% (cited from knowledge; gov.uk 403 via proxy)
VAT Notice 733 LCT test: relevant goods inc VAT < 2% of flat-rate turnover; hand 2% x 60,000 = 1,200
VAT Notice 733 capital expenditure goods >= £2,000 inc VAT single purchase
HMRC flat rate percentages table (from 1 April 2017), recalled; spot-checked all 52 rows
checks.expected: all HMRC categories including Catering 12.5% and Any other activity 12%

checks.method: VAT Notice 733: must leave when total income inc VAT exceeds £230,000
checks.expected: headline does not recommend FRS for a business that must leave
checks.observed: headline 'Flat Rate Scheme leaves £4,200.00 a year more'; join/leave finding shown separately

checks.what: page 'Covers ... 1% first-year discount ... join and leave turnover limits'
checks.observed: discount withheld from LCT, leave limit not applied

checks.command: grep -n 'No warranty\|Not tax advice' index.html calc.mjs

checks.observed: proxy 403 CONNECT rejected; not checked live

defects.what: First-year 1% discount is not applied to the 16.5% limited cost trader rate (HMRC allows 15.5% in the first year of registration). Overstates FRS cost by 1% of gross turnover and can flip the verdict: 60k IT consultant, goods 300, other 1,000, first year shows 'Standard wins by £140' when FRS wins by £580. A test (calc.test.mjs:26-28) pins the wrong rule.
Sector table omits 'Catering services including restaurants and takeaways' (12.5%) and 'Any other activity not listed elsewhere' (12%); a restaurant cannot select its trade.

Leave limit not modelled: a business at £240,000 VAT-inclusive is told 'Flat Rate Scheme wins by £4,200' in the headline; the £230k test (and the £191,500 exception) only appears as text inside the join finding.
3 of 5 seeded mutants survive: LCT and capital boundaries and the sector table are untested against a source.
Page claims it 'Covers' the 1% discount and the leave limit; README says you will 'know whether to join (or leave)'. Both overstate given the defects above.
LCT test is annual only; HMRC applies it per return period (£250 a quarter), so lumpy goods purchases are misjudged. Relevant-goods note omits vehicle parts and the goods-for-resale/hire exclusion.

verdict: A small, tidy FRS-vs-standard calculator whose arithmetic is right (builder, LCT 2% boundary and £2,000 capital boundary all recompute exactly) and whose existing sector rates match HMRC's table, but a VAT adviser would not sign it off: it withholds the first-year 1% from the 16.5% limited cost rate, which flips the verdict for exactly the newly registered contractors it targets; two HMRC sectors (catering, any other activity) are missing; and the headline recommends FRS to a business over the £230k leave limit. 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive. Correctness, claims and verification are all 2, so it does not meet the bar; finished-ness is 2.
